messages:
maya: heads up — deploybot just flagged a release-notes inconsistency for v3.7.1. the embedding-compatibility note was removed but routing still assumes it. deploybot suggested an auto-revert.

deploy-bot: AUTO-ROLLBACK SUGGESTION: p95 error spike 5.2% on /generate since rollout start. Recommend revert to v3.7.0 for hosted. (reason: manifest mismatch) :warning:

henry: auto-reverts are OK for hosted but we CANNOT auto-revert dedicated pools — several customers are pinned to v3.7.1 in Dedicated and will break. we need operator approval.

kia: agreed. this is a divergence between hosted and dedicated. propose: targeted revert for hosted only + flip release flag for routing to exclude Dedicated pools. manual approval for any change that touches dedicated.

elliot-oncall: what commands are we running for the hosted rollback? need a short runbook so oncall can execute quickly.

maya: quick command snippet for hosted rollback (run in infra-prod):
```
# rollback hosted route to v3.7.0
infractl rollout service/redwood-hosted --target-version v3.7.0 --scope hosted-only --reason "release-notes mismatch auto-fallback"
# freeze routing to dedicated pools
infractl config set routing.block_dedicated_rollout true --env prod
```

henry: couple of checks before we run: confirm no active long-running jobs on hosted that depend on v3.7.1, and ensure traffic-slice personalizations are saved. also patch the release manifest to restore the embedding flag or document the breaking change.

release-manager: I'll update the release notes immediately and add a clear breaking-change bullet for embedding compatibility. drafting an addendum to push to the docs site + changelog.

cs-alex: customer-success will prepare an outbound for any Dedicated customers pinned to v3.7.1. we'll include rollback risk, timeline, and mitigation steps. ask: can we avoid any forced change to their pools?

kia: yes — the plan explicitly avoids touching Dedicated pools. we only flip the hosted route and set the config flag to prevent automated rollouts for dedicated. ops will do manual steps for dedicated if needed.

elliot-oncall: runbook checklist for this thread (one-line items):
```
- confirm deploybot telemetry and error windows (maya)
- quiesce non-critical hosted background jobs (henry)
- execute hosted rollback command (oncall)
- set routing.block_dedicated_rollout=true (oncall)
- validate p95/p99 and error rates for 15m post-rollback (observability)
- update release notes + publish addendum (release-manager)
- send cs outbound to pinned Dedicated customers (cs-alex)
- open follow-up ticket to fix manifest & add test that catches the manifest mismatch (eng-releases backlog)
```

deploy-bot: action queued: manual-approval-required for rollback-hosted. use `/deploy approve 5987654321` to proceed.

maya: approving now — `/deploy approve 5987654321` :white_check_mark:

elliot-oncall: executing rollback in 2m. ping here when done.

(2 minutes later)
elliot-oncall: hosted rollback completed. p95 dropped back to baseline within 6m. error spike cleared. observability shows steady-state.

henry: great. thanks. leaving the dedicated flag set — ops please don't unset until we have manifest fix.

release-manager: addendum published: https://docs.redwood.ai/changelog/v3.7.1-addendum — included mitigation steps and ETA for manifest fix.

cs-alex: outbound queued to pinned customers, copy to legal + security. template attached in thread.

maya: good job everyone. post-mortem ticket created: ENG-ROLL-7421. we'll schedule a short sit-down tomorrow to tighten the release manifest validation. :thumbsup:
